data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0/virtio) has wedged — its TX queue repeatedly hits watchdog timeouts and the link flaps — so even though the ISP modem re-registered and is OPERATIONAL, gw.lan cannot send anything onto the WAN segment (gateway ARP incomplete), which is why the internet stayed down despite the WAN reloads.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0/virtio) has wedged — its TX queue repeatedly hits watchdog timeouts and the link flaps — so even though the ISP modem re-registered and is OPERATIONAL, gw.lan cannot send anything onto the WAN segment (gateway ARP incomplete), which is why the internet stayed down despite the WAN reloads.
evidence: dmesg -a: repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP', indicating a stalled transmit queue and link resets on the WAN NIC.
netstat -i: vtnet0 shows Oerrs=48211 (output errors) while Ipkts/Ipkts flow continues; LAN vtnet1 has 0 errors.
arp -a -n: default-gateway/MAC entry for 198.51.100.1 shows '(incomplete)' — address resolution to the ISP CPE never completes, i.e. L2 failure on the WAN link.
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1: 'No buffer space available' / 100% loss to the ISP gateway, yet ping to LAN host 10.20.0.9 succeeds (local services fine).
ifconfig vtnet0 / netstat -rn: interface UP with valid DHCP lease (198.51.100.27, expire 2026/3/6) and correct default route via 198.51.100.1 — so config/lease are not at fault.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl + state.json: watchdog performed 4 reloads this outage (12 in 24h, hit max_reloads_24h=12), each rc=0, none restored connectivity; final decision at 03:30 was action=none reason=reload_cap.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl + modem-metrics.jsonl: cable modem logged 'registration complete' at 02:28 and reports cm_status OPERATIONAL with good SNR (~37.7 dB) — the provider/CPE side recovered, isolating the persistent fault to gw.lan's WAN NIC.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 WAN NIC/driver. The WAN reload path is exhausted (12/24h cap reached) and demonstrably ineffective against a driver-level TX hang, and the modem itself is already re-registered/OPERATIONAL so a modem power-cycle would not help. A full reboot clears the wedged queue and restores the datapath; afterward, verify the gateway pings and ARP resolves, and consider a NIC/driver update or replacement if watchdog timeouts recur.
data.detail: WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit queue hangs / driver watchdog timeouts
